evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: For 'Отмена последней операции', the learner can pathlib-based scanning with symlink/permission-error handling, narrow exception handling philosophy, extension-based classification, collision-safe planning, apply_plan() executor, JSON manifest + undo, chunked SHA-256 duplicate detection with byte-level confirmation, read-only tomllib config overlay.

scan() recursively walks via iterdir()/is_dir()/is_file()/is_symlink()/stat(), skips symlinks entirely (never followed, both to files and directories), skips PermissionError/FileNotFoundError/OSError per-directory with a warning log rather than aborting the whole scan -- confirmed: read projects/python/safesort/src/safesort/scanner.py in full; matches the chapter's code samples exactly; behavior verified indirectly via the passing test_scanner.py suite (part of the 88/88 passing run)

`except Exception: pass` is explicitly called out as 'not a solution' — narrow except clauses (PermissionError, FileNotFoundError, OSError) used throughout instead -- confirmed: grepped the entire real safesort/src/ tree and scripts/build_chapter_23.py — zero occurrences of a broad `except Exception` catch anywhere in the actual source code; the only 'except Exception' text in the whole chapter is the pedagogical warning against doing it

SHA-256 duplicate detection staged as size-prefilter -> chunked hashlib.sha256() digest -> byte-by-byte files_equal() confirmation before reporting a group; chunked reads never load a whole file into memory -- confirmed: read duplicates.py in full — sha256_stream()/sha256_file()/files_equal()/find_duplicates() implement exactly this staged algorithm with a documented DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE=1MiB; docstring explicitly states a digest match alone is 'never the final answer'; notebook 23-17-sha256.ipynb and 23-18-duplicaty.ipynb executed cleanly and produced correct digests/groupings

apply_plan() re-checks `destination.exists() or destination.is_symlink()` immediately before each move (not just at plan time), because `shutil.move()`/`os.rename()` on POSIX would otherwise silently overwrite a file that appeared after planning; a failed move in the middle of a batch does not roll back already-completed moves and is explicitly NOT claimed to be a database-style transaction -- confirmed: read executor.py in full, matches exactly; the chapter's warning callout ('Партия перемещений — не транзакция базы данных') is honest and technically accurate — no false atomicity claim anywhe

undo() only reverses moves recorded with completed=True, refuses to restore (records a conflict, continues with the rest) if something now exists at the original source path, never overwrites silently -- confirmed: read manifest.py's undo() in full, matches; notebook 23-16-undo.ipynb executed cleanly and demonstrated a real move+manifest-write+undo round-trip with correct restoration; 23-20-test-peremeshenie.ipynb also demonstrates the undo-refuses-to-overwrite-conflict test passing

Manifest is a JSON file at `<root>/.safesort/history/<operation_id>.json`, read back via read_manifest() which raises a clear ManifestError (not a raw traceback) on missing/invalid/malformed data -- confirmed accurate, matches manifest.py exactly

Config file (`safesort.toml`) is read via stdlib `tomllib.load()` and explicitly documented/stated as read-only: 'SafeSort never writes TOML' (config.py module docstring, line 10) and the chapter's own text at line ~4342 says the same -- confirmed accurate on both sides — the real config.py module docstring literally states this, and grepped the entire build_chapter_23.py for tomli_w/tomlkit/any TOML-write claim: NONE found anywhere. This is exactly the correct behavior per Python 3.11+ stdlib (tomllib is read-only); the chapter never claims otherwise. Notebook 23-19-toml-config.ipynb executed

Directory scanning excludes destination dir + `.safesort` state dir + configured excludes dynamically, so repeated scan/plan/apply never reprocesses already-sorted files or SafeSort's own manifests -- confirmed: Config.excluded_names() in config.py matches exactly; notebook 23-10-isklyucheniya.ipynb confirms the exclusion set at runtime
